newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks barely changed ahead of economic data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks barely changed ahead of economic data.

text.p: U.S. stocks were barely changed in early trading ahead of key U.S. economic data due for release Wednesday and Thursday, although firmer bonds offered some underpinning, analysts said.
An upside move on the Dow's opening fizzled, leaving the benchmark indicator fluctuating between the negative and positive columns in early trading.

"I am a little surprised the initial rally did not hold," Alfred Kugel, Stein Roe & Farnham's senior investment strategist said. "I don't think it's anything significant. We don't have any important news on the economy until tomorrow."
The Dow Jones Industrial average was up 13.94 at 8076.05, with the Nasdaq composite up 11.14 at 1597.88.
The long bond was up 18/32 to a 6.60 percent yield.
Goldman Sachs' Abby Joseph Cohen said in a newsletter that stock prices were characterized by a staircase pattern -- quantum upward steps were followed by a choppy trading range.
"The fundamentals of solid profit growth and mild inflation remain intact and will determine the future direction of stock prices," Cohen said. "There is no recession in our forecast."

Data released Tuesday indicated that U.S. second quarter non-farm productivity rose 0.6 percent, close to analysts' expectations, while unit labor costs for the same period were up 2.4 percent, softer than expected.
But analysts said the market was still largely focused on Wednesday's key U.S. retail sales and producer prices for July, followed by Thursday's consumer prices.
